question: A 47-year-old man, with a history of a right parotid pleomorphic adenoma, treated with surgery (extrafacial parotidectomy) 6 months ago, who came to our clinic because he presented pain during the mastication with sweating and reddening of the skin of the preauricular region. What treatment would be the one of choice?

options.opa: Total parotidectomy enlarged when suspicion of tumor recurrence.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: History of right parotid pleomorphic adenoma -> previous surgery (extrafacial parotidectomy) -> current pain during mastication with sweating and reddening of the skin of the preauricular region -> possible nerve damage or irritation -> consider neuropathic pain as a cause -> Pregabalin may help manage neuropathic pain -> Pregabalin -> 70%

CHAIN: Pain during mastication with sweating and reddening of the skin of the preauricular region -> possible trigeminal neuralgia -> Injection of intradermal botulinum toxin can be considered for trigeminal neuralgia -> Injection of intradermal botulinum toxin -> 60%

CHAIN: Pain during mastication with sweating and reddening of the skin of the preauricular region -> signs of infection or inflammation -> consider broad spectrum antibiotic therapy -> Broad spectrum antibiotic therapy -> 80%
enhanced_information: For the 47-year-old man with a history of right parotid pleomorphic adenoma and current pain during mastication with sweating and reddening of the skin of the preauricular region, the treatment of choice should be total parotidectomy if there is suspicion of tumor recurrence. This aligns with the standard approach for managing recurrent pleomorphic adenoma. Pregabalin, injection of intradermal botulinum toxin, and broad spectrum antibiotic therapy are not the recommended treatments in this context.
analysis: The core medical principle here is to consider the possibility of tumor recurrence in a patient with a history of pleomorphic adenoma presenting with pain during mastication, sweating, and reddening of the skin in the preauricular region. The treatment of choice in this scenario is total parotidectomy if there is suspicion of tumor recurrence, as it aligns with the standard approach for managing recurrent pleomorphic adenoma.
